messages:
marta: Heads-up — customer X just hit a critical path where internal billing and ingestion traffic needs short bursts above org quota for a few seconds. They want "priority" keys that can preempt other low-priority requests for microbursts. Any thoughts on safety/implementation?

sam: hmm. priority keys + preemption sounds risky for fairness. how would we prevent a noisy customer from claiming priority and starving others? :thinking_face:

linh: We could make priority explicit per-key and require an enterprise flag + contract. Also only allow preemption for requests tagged P0 with a strict short window (eg 5s) and a hard cap.

alex: Two implementation choices: (A) router-level fast decision: consult an allowlist + local token cache and preempt by temporarily lowering tokens on low-priority buckets. Very low latency but distributed consistency pain. (B) central quota service: one canonical place to revoke/grant tokens, easier visibility but adds RPC latency.

jordan: if we go with preemption we need metrics: preemption_count, tokens_stolen, victim_org, preemption_latency. Also a dashboard that shows preemption events linked to invoices and SLA impacts.

sam: Also consider alternative: "burst-exempt credits" model. Give priority keys a separate short-lived credit bucket that refills slowly. That way they don't steal from others, they just draw from their credits. Simpler for fairness.

marta: good point. credits avoid cross-org theft. but credits can be gamed if issuance is too generous. we need issuance policy and an audit trail.

linh: From runtime perspective I prefer credits implemented in the router cache: store (org_id, credit_balance, last_refill). Router can allow a burst if credit_balance > 0 without a roundtrip. Central service reconciles eventually.

alex: router cache + central reconciler is reasonable. edge fast path for latency-critical paths, fall back to central check for large bursts. we must ensure monotonic counters so we don't double-spend on failover.

marta: UX question: console needs a toggle per-api-key: "Allow short priority bursts" and a mandatory justification field for audit. Also show recent preemption/burst events on key detail page.

jordan: add feature-level guardrails: max_burst_tokens, burst_window_secs, and a dynamic decay to avoid long-term privilege. Also require a billing rule: bursts are billable at a premium or deducted from reserved capacity.

sam: security angle: require a signed admin approval for any priority enablement. Also limit the number of priority keys per org to prevent scope creep.

marta: operational concerns: when preemption happens we should degrade gracefully — return 429 with Retry-After when victim org can't be preempted further, not silently slow the request. Also emit detailed traces for the trace ID in the console.

linh: quick config sketch: 
```
api_key: ak_01XYZ
priority: true
burst: {
  enabled: true
  max_tokens: 200
  window_secs: 10
  refill_rate_per_min: 30
  audit_required: true
}
```

alex: code notes: we need atomic decrement semantics for credit draw on the router. Use a compare-and-swap against cached counter or local LMDB + lease. If router fails, central service must reconcile and mark retries.

jordan: dashboard widgets to add: time series of burst_consumption, top priority keys by consumption, 429s caused by preemption, and a daily audit export.

deploy-bot: CI: burst-credits prototype branch passed unit tests, integration tests queued. Build #7821 started.

marta: next steps: 1) sam + linh draft a short design doc comparing credits vs preemption (due EOW). 2) alex to prototype router cache atomic draw + reconciler (PR WIP). 3) jordan to draft dashboard spec and metrics (eta 3 days). 4) ops guard rails: require admin sign-off flow (marta to coordinate).

sam: i'll own the design doc. will include abuse scenarios and billing models.

linh: i'll start the router prototype and write the cache eviction/lease plan.

alex: will spike on CAS in the router and put up an RFC.

jordan: will mock up the console UX + a sample CSV audit export.

marta: thanks. one more: make the feature flag default-off and rollout behind canary so we can measure impact on tail latency before wide enablement. :+1:

sam: ack. i'll include a canary plan in the doc.

marta: great. closing loop — ping me once PRs exist and i'll open a rollout ticket and coordinate with sales for any customer-specific approvals.

linh: noted.

alex: pinged on the RFC channel when I have the prototype.

deploy-bot: Build #7821: integration tests queued (burst-credits/prototype).

marta: thanks team — moving this to a tracked design thread.
